claim_text: Sinusoidal positional encoding uses sin(pos / 10000^{2i/d}), so nearby positions have a similar encoding.

spec.explain: Toy illustration of sinusoidal positional encoding from 1706.03762. Watch the ratio number: below 1 nearby positions share encoding, above 1 they separate along the similarity curve.

questions.q: Set i to 0: what happens to the neighbors? Do you expect positions one apart to look alike?
Set i to 4: what happens to the wavelength?
Set seq to 100: what happens to the ratio?
Set d to 512: what happens to the wavelength?
